subject: Logic
title: Valid vs Sound
description: Learn Valid vs Sound in one minute.

hook.text: All cats can fly. Mittens is a cat. Therefore Mittens can fly. Logically valid—but obviously absurd.

buildup.text: Validity means the conclusion follows from the premises. It says nothing about whether the premises are true.

discovery.text: Soundness is stronger: a sound argument is valid AND has true premises. That's the gold standard.

twist.text: Many persuasive arguments are valid but unsound—the logic works, but the starting facts are wrong.

climax.text: Always check both: does the logic hold, and are the premises actually true?

punchline.text: Valid logic, false start, wrong finish.

quiz.question: What makes an argument sound?
options: It is valid and has true premises
